title: Probabilistic latency-quality landscape sampling for batching + KV-cache configs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: We need a lightweight, probabilistic sampling harness that maps the joint latency-vs-quality distribution across the configuration space of microbatch sizes, KV-cache TTLs, and cache hit heuristics. Existing grid sweeps are costly and miss low-probability but high-impact regions (e.g., long-tail prompts that cause cache poisoning or severe quality regressions under specific microbatch alignments). This ticket implements a sampling-driven evaluator that prioritizes exploration of risky configuration combinations, produces uncertainty estimates per config, and surfaces regression signals tied to model and config changes.
acceptance_criteria: A sampling harness that runs within existing eval infra and returns per-config estimates of median latency, 95th percentile latency, and quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR or model-specific scorer)
Uncertainty intervals (95% CI) computed for each metric using bootstrap or Bayesian approximations
Risk score derived from latency tail * negative quality delta that ranks configs for investigation
Integration with regression-monitoring: when risk score delta vs baseline exceeds threshold, create alert and attach representative traces and seed prompts
End-to-end run for 30 candidate configs on the 'chat-heavy' slice within 8 wall-clock hours on standard eval cluster
plan_steps: Design sampling strategy: stratified random + adaptive oversampling of previously high-variance regions
Implement config encoding and scheduler to emit microbatch+TTL+heuristic combinations to workers
Extend eval worker to capture per-request quality score via eval hooks and attach token-level latency traces
Implement uncertainty estimator (bootstrap with 200 resamples) and risk scoring formula
Integrate with alerts: post a regression-ticket to Linear API and upload artifact links (top-k prompts, traces) to Confluence
Run pilot across three model families (open-gpt-xx, rdl-medium, rdl-large) and collect baseline
Review pilot results with PM/Design; iterate thresholds and sampling hyperparams
eval_dataset: mix of 10k prompts: 60% conversational/dialogue (short/long-turn), 20% code/structured-output, 20% knowledge-dense prompts; seeded with 500 known edge prompts that previously caused cache-related quality issues
alerts: Risk score increase > 0.2 (relative) triggers a regression-ticket with top 10 offending prompts and traces
p95_latency increase > 25% with customer_impact "medium" or higher sends page to infra-oncall
quality delta < -0.03 (absolute) for any config flagged as production toggled config creates a blocking alert
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete on sampling strategies. Tried pure Bayesian optimization but convergence to low-variance regions; settled on stratified sampling with adaptive oversampling of bins that exceed variance threshold.
2026-03-04: Added per-request evaluator hook. Worker now emits quality score and latency trace to S3 prefix for later aggregation. Small perf overhead (~1.8%) observed in eval worker.

2026-03-07: Pilot run started on rdl-medium for 12 candidate configs. Initial results show one config (microbatch=32, TTL=12s, heuristic=aggressive) with high p95 and a negative quality delta on code prompts. Captured top 25 offending prompts for triage.

2026-03-10: Implemented bootstrap uncertainty estimator. End-to-end pipeline can produce metrics and risk scores; starting integration tests with regression-monitoring alert rules. Pausing to validate signal false-positive rate on synthetic stable workloads.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: wider sampling reduces per-run depth; we bias sampling toward higher variance bins to catch rare regressions without exhaustive grid search.
We should avoid enabling the full production KV-cache heuristics in pilot (use a diagnostic-mode to reproduce hit/miss behavior while keeping test isolation).
Follow-up: if risk scoring proves useful, add continuous nightly runs and a dashboard in Console showing config risk heatmap per model family.
